nodes.question: How can IoT devices and digital platforms be utilized to capture data for specific product transactions?
nodes.answer: IoT devices and digital platforms can be used to capture data for specific product transactions, as suggested by Alves et al., 2022 and Franck et al., 2022. This can enable the possible tracking of product circularity and improve end-of-life management.

nodes.question: How does the Industry Aligned Action Plan propose to scale circular systems according to Franck et al. (2022)?
nodes.answer: The Industry Aligned Action Plan proposes to scale circular systems through the implementation of digital IDs, which will enable the tracking and tracing of materials and products throughout their lifecycle, promoting a more sustainable and circular economy.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Digitalization in circular economy_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What improvements do digital technologies (DTs) provide in the context of the Life Cycle Inventory phase?
nodes.answer: DTs improve the trustworthiness of the inventory and enhance data transparency and traceability, which are critical for circular economy practices.
nodes.paragraph: However, even if DTs can facilitate and improve the trustworthiness of the inventory, they can also lead to an increase in complex- ity because more competencies are needed, it is more difficult to control data collection and elaboration, and more social interactions along the supply chain are needed. At the same time, DTs can reduce flexibility because further improvements are blocked, interfaces can be rigid to connect, and technical and normative updates can be more difficult to implement. Conclusions DTs improve the development of the Life Cycle Inventory phase, particularly in the context of the circular economy. However, they also introduce new complexities and challenges. The use of blockchain, digital twins, and loT sensors, for instance, has significantly improved data transparency and traceability, which are critical for circular economy practices, but complexity and training requirements can limit their benefits, so careful consideration must be given to their implementation to maximise benefits and minimise drawbacks. nodes.question: How do digital technologies enhance sustainability in supply chains?
nodes.answer: The use of digital technologies promotes a more efficient use of resources, enhancing the sustainability and circularity of supply chains.

Specifically, DTs optimise the data acquisition, collection, and management pro- cesses, ensuring greater transparency and traceability (Zhang et al. 2020; Carri res et al. 2021; Mogos and Fragapane 2022; Sica et al. 2022). By implementing advanced systems, they also increase the sharing processes and security of data trans- mission (Huang et al. 2020 ; Sica et al. 2022 ; Dervishaj and Gudmundsson 2024). For instance, the inventory phase can benefit from digital technologies by gathering complete and accurate data, supporting decision-makers in identifying effec- tive solutions for reducing environmental impact (Zhang et al. 2020). nodes.question: What are the benefits of integrating digital technologies into LCA?
nodes.answer: The integration boosts innovation in production processes and improves corporate sustainability, fostering the digital and circular transition.

This approach boosts innovation in production processes and improves corporate sustainability, fostering the twin digi - tal and circular transition (Nascimento et al. 2019; Bai et al. 2020 ; Bocken et al. 2023). Despite the benefits, integrating digital technologies into LCA is a complex process as it is still at an early stage of study and implementation (Wang et al. 2019; Sica et al. 2022). The main barriers to improvements in these terms include the need for advanced technical skills to implement and manage these technologies, high initial costs associated with the adoption of new digital infrastructure, and resistance to change within organisations (Farooque et al. 2020; Ruggieri et al. 2020). In addition, the lack of standardi- sation and interoperability between different digital tools and platforms can complicate data integration and hinder the effec- tiveness of assessments (Ghita et al. 2021 ). nodes.question: How can digital technologies catalyse business model innovation for circular economy according to Santa et al. (2021)?

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Digitalization in circular economy_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the concept of sustainable digitalization in industry?
nodes.answer: Sustainable digitalization refers to using digital technologies to enhance sustainability by reducing environmental impact, lowering post-consumer textile wastes, and increasing resource efficiency.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Digitalization in circular economy_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some environmental benefits of sustainable digitalization?
nodes.answer: Environmental benefits of sustainable digitalization include environmental protection, climate change mitigation, nature conservation, circular economy practices, and overall sustainability for the environment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Digitalization in circular economy_qna_010
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How is company management impacted by sustainable digitalization?
nodes.answer: Better company management with sustainable digitalization leads to cost savings, increased effectiveness, and improved competitiveness in the industry.

nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Can digitalization favour the emergence of innovative and sustainable business models, according to one of the references?
nodes.answer: Yes, according to Saccharin et al. (2021), digitalization can favour the emergence of innovative and sustainable business models, as explored in the automotive sector.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Digitalization in circular economy_qna_012
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can sustainable digitalization facilitate a green transition according to Editor (2022)?
nodes.answer: According to Editor (2022), sustainable digitalization can help facilitate a green transition by reducing environmental impact or increasing resource efficiency.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Digitalization in circular economy_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can digitalization contribute to creating a smart green planet?
nodes.answer: Digitalization can contribute to creating a smart green planet by promoting the adoption of renewable energy sources, optimizing resource utilization through smart technologies, and fostering sustainable practices across various sectors through data analytics and automation.

nodes.question: How can digitalization and Industry 4.0 technologies contribute to monitoring sustainability in the ceramic industry?
nodes.answer: Digitalization and Industry 4.0 technologies can help develop key performance indicators for monitoring sustainability in the ceramic industry more effectively.

nodes.answer: Gupta et al. (2019) focus on the stakeholder perspective of circular economy and big data analytics, exploring the intersection of these two concepts.

nodes.question: Which countries have been identified as making slower progress in transitioning towards circularity according to Mazer-Wierzbicka (2021)?
nodes.answer: Cyprus, Hungary, and Bulgaria have been highlighted as progressing at a slower pace in transitioning towards circularity compared to countries like the Netherlands, Germany, and Belgium.
